meta.title: TORFL B2 Certificate Level 2 — Russian
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Russian → English (see the Russian, recall the meaning) and English → Russian (see an English meaning, recall the Russian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for the Certificate Level 2 level (Второй сертификационный уровень, ТРКИ-2) of TORFL, the Test of Russian as a Foreign Language (ТРКИ), the Russian state examination, which corresponds to CEFR B2. TORFL's Certificate Level 2 level is aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main ideas of complex text on both concrete and abstract topics' — a learner here is able to interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction with native speakers quite possible, and to produce clear, detailed text on a wide range of subjects, explaining a viewpoint on a topical issue with the advantages and disadvantages of various options. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: TORFL's lexical minimum for each level is published as a book under copyright rather than as an open list, so this deck is not the exam board's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 186 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — the language of argument (advantages and drawbacks, conclusions, objections, and the connectives that join them), abstract concepts, society and politics, the economy, science and technology, the environment, culture and the arts, the media, education and expertise, medicine, character and the mind, and the verbs, adjectives and adverbs of analysis and judgement — and the other 1314 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Russian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case and every tense added together, since a list of word forms ranks книгу above книга. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword and every form is printed with its stress mark, as Russian dictionaries for learners print them, because Russian stress is free and moves (рука́, ру́ку) and nothing in the spelling shows it; the example sentences are printed as they were written, without stress. 284 of the verbs are taught as aspect pairs on one card, imperfective first (де́лать / сде́лать), each with its own conjugation, since a Russian verb is learnt as a pair; the verbs of motion that make round trips (ходи́ть, е́здить) are cards of their own beside идти́ and е́хать, because the difference is the lesson. The 834 nouns show their gender, their genitive singular and their nominative plural, from which the rest of the declension follows, and every word that inflects has its whole table behind the All forms fold. 7 of the entries are set phrases rather than single words — то есть, таким образом, в основном. Real example sentences come with 1490 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 1450 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. There is no transliteration: learn the alphabet first with the Russian alphabet deck, which is the first deck in this collection. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, forms, stress and aspect: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

fields.English:
adverb
  • differently, in a different way; otherwise
  • otherwise, else, or else
fields.Examples:
В этот раз всё будет иначе.
This time, it will be different.
В следующий раз будем делать иначе.
Next time, we'll do this differently.
Я бы сделал это совсем иначе.
I'd do it completely differently.

fields.English:
adverb
apparently, obviously
fields.Examples:
Очевидно, что тебе больше не интересно.
It's obvious that you're no longer interested.
Я думал, что это уже очевидно.
I thought that was already obvious.
Возможно, это было не так очевидно.
Maybe it was not so obvious.
